cohort: The study included 120 low-risk pregnant patients at term, categorized into a group with low amniotic fluid index (AFI <= 5 cm) and a control group with standard AFI (> 5 cm).
finding: Patients with low AFI had a significantly higher rate of neonatal complications including lower Apgar scores at 5 minutes, increased need for NICU admission, low birth weight, and meconium aspiration compared to patients with standard AFI.
mod_finding: No significant difference was observed between cases and controls regarding C-section delivery (30% vs 25%).
followup_time: 5 minutes (Apgar score at 5 minutes), neonatal period (NICU admission, low birth weight, meconium aspiration, respiratory distress)
birth_weight: N/A (low birth weight was an outcome, not an inclusion criteria weight)
